records.title: OCS / Mitie
records.fact: OCS agreed a recommended cash offer for Mitie in July. Mitie's 19 November interim results reported 99.7% shareholder support and two of three regulatory clearances. CMA Phase 1 began on 18 November.
records.analysis: Overlapping service contracts may require close analysis of customers’ alternatives, bidding patterns and local or national market definition. Counsel should separate commercial closing conditions from the regulator’s timetable.
records.watch: Read the latest CMA case update before relying on this snapshot.
records.structure: Recommended all-cash acquisition via scheme of arrangement.

values.label: Fully diluted acquisition value, including final dividend
FY26 final dividend per share (paid separately)

records.financing: Specific financing terms have not been verified for this dossier.
records.regulatory: The published Phase 1 decision deadline is 20 January 2027, subject to extension. Shareholder support is not regulatory approval.

timeline.event: Mitie reported approval progress and expected Q1 2027 completion

records.legalWork: Review the scheme conditions and court timetable; map regulatory clearance conditions and long-stop mechanics; evaluate overlapping facilities services using customer and bidding data. Separate dividend treatment from the headline cash offer.
records.interview: Why can an overwhelmingly approved scheme remain pending? Explain the distinction between shareholder approval, court sanction and competition clearance.

records.title: McCormick / Unilever Foods
records.fact: Unilever announced the Foods combination on 31 March. Its October update said the transaction remained on track; on 11 November the CMA found potential competition concerns requiring an acceptable remedy to avoid a Phase 2 referral.
records.analysis: The case illustrates how anticipated competition remedies can change the economic perimeter of a deal. A buyer must test whether any divestment would undermine the investment thesis or financing model.
records.watch: Check subsequent decisions and any published commitments; this is not a live status guarantee.
records.structure: Separation of Unilever Foods and combination with McCormick via a Reverse Morris Trust structure.
records.financing: The announcement identifies Citi, Goldman Sachs Bank USA and Morgan Stanley Senior Funding as bridge financing providers; the intended permanent funding includes new debt and cash.
records.regulatory: CMA Phase 1 concerns are not a prohibition. Shareholder approval, regulatory clearances and separation conditions remain relevant.
records.legalWork: Carve-out perimeter, transition services, tax structuring, financing commitments and remedy allocation should be negotiated together. Assess whether a required divestment would undermine the economics of the combined foods business.
records.interview: How does a carve-out differ from a simple share acquisition, and what happens to the financing case if competition remedies remove profitable brands?

records.title: Sky / ITV Media and Entertainment
records.fact: A public-interest intervention notice was issued on 4 November 2026 in connection with Sky UK's proposed purchase of ITV M&E Holdings. The published timetable identifies 27 January 2027 for CMA and Ofcom reports to the Secretary of State.
records.analysis: Media acquisitions may face scrutiny beyond ordinary competition effects, including plurality of news views. Regulatory allocation and long-stop dates become important negotiation points.
records.watch: 27 January 2027: published reporting deadline; check for extensions.
records.structure: Proposed acquisition of ITV media and entertainment business; detailed definitive terms not established here.
records.regulatory: Section 42 Enterprise Act 2002 intervention requires separate reports from CMA and Ofcom. The notice addresses media plurality and free expression. A proposed extension to on-demand programming is not treated as enacted law.

timeline.event: Secretary of State indicated intention to intervene

records.legalWork: Map media ownership and audiences, assess competition and public-interest requirements separately, allocate risk of conditions and extensions, and plan communications without prejudging the Secretary of State's decision.
records.interview: How can a merger with limited conventional competition concerns still face a public-interest review?

records.title: Co-operative Group / Southern Co-operative
records.fact: The CMA accepted commitments on 5 November 2026 to resolve its concerns over the already-completed acquisition without a Phase 2 reference.
records.analysis: Completion does not necessarily end UK merger risk. A buyer completing before clearance may face restrictions on integration or remedial commitments; transaction documents should allocate these risks explicitly.
records.watch: Check the final undertakings and implementation updates.
records.structure: Completed acquisition reviewed by the CMA.
records.regulatory: Phase 1 concerns resolved through undertakings in lieu accepted 5 November 2026. This is a remedy decision, not unconditional clearance.
records.legalWork: Post-closing integration controls and remedy compliance need an owner, deadlines and documentary evidence. Review final undertakings before specifying affected assets or operational commitments.
records.interview: What risks arise from closing a UK merger before CMA clearance?

records.title: Vodafone UK / Three UK
records.fact: The combination completed on 31 May 2025 with Vodafone initially holding 51%. Vodafone subsequently announced acquisition of CK Hutchison's remaining 49%, taking full ownership; the £4.3bn figure relates to that later transaction, not the original merger.
records.analysis: A network merger can create scale benefits but reduce competitive pressure. Commitments on investment and customer outcomes may affect integration economics and ongoing compliance long after closing.
records.watch: CMA monitoring reports and performance against the commitments.
records.structure: Contribution of UK mobile businesses with different debt amounts to produce initial 51:49 ownership, without cash consideration on original combination.
records.financing: The later stake purchase was funded from existing cash resources, according to Vodafone.
records.regulatory: CMA commitments relate to the original network combination; the subsequent ownership acquisition is a distinct event.
records.legalWork: For the original combination, separate contribution agreements, governance and network commitments from later share acquisition documentation. Monitor enforceable commitments and distinguish projected synergies from realised benefits.
records.interview: Why is the £4.3bn buyout not the value of the original Vodafone/Three merger?

records.title: Microsoft / Activision Blizzard (restructured)
records.fact: After opposing the original transaction, the CMA cleared a revised structure in October 2023 involving the transfer of certain cloud-streaming rights to Ubisoft.
records.analysis: Control over distribution rights can matter as much as ownership of the target. A carve-out may create licensing, transitional services and intellectual property issues that need separate documentation.
records.watch: Compare the original prohibition with the revised transaction; do not treat the decisions as contradictory on identical facts.
records.structure: Revised acquisition excludes non-EEA cloud streaming rights transferred to Ubisoft.
records.regulatory: The revised deal was allowed with enforceable undertakings following prohibition of the original proposal.
records.legalWork: Define IP and licensing perimeter, territory, duration and technical obligations; negotiate enforceability of rights transfers and assess interaction with other jurisdictions' commitments.
records.interview: Why might transferring cloud distribution rights address competition concerns more effectively than behavioural promises?

records.title: Nationwide / Virgin Money
records.fact: The CMA cleared the proposed acquisition on 19 July 2024; Virgin Money later confirmed FCA and PRA approval. Nationwide confirms completion on 1 October 2024. A separate legal transfer of Virgin Money's business to Nationwide completed on 2 April 2026.
records.analysis: Bank acquisitions may involve separate prudential and competition workstreams. Clearance from one authority does not establish satisfaction of all conditions or completion.
records.watch: Distinguish the original share acquisition from the later business transfer and integration.
records.structure: Acquisition of Virgin Money followed by a distinct legal transfer of its business.
records.regulatory: Competition, prudential and conduct approvals are separate; the legal business transfer is not the same as completion of the share acquisition.
records.legalWork: Review regulated change-of-control requirements, deposit and customer communications, operational resilience and integration dependencies; distinguish acquisition closing from later business-transfer mechanics.
records.interview: Why might a bank acquisition take multiple regulatory and legal workstreams after completion?

records.title: Bank Rate rises to 4%
records.fact: At the meeting ending 4 November 2026, the MPC voted 8–1 to raise Bank Rate by 25 basis points to 4%.
records.analysis: Floating-rate borrowers may face higher debt service. Acquisition models should revisit interest cover, covenant headroom and refinancing assumptions; fixed-rate borrowers may be less immediately affected.
records.watch: Next MPC decision, lender pricing and borrower hedging requirements.

records.title: October inflation release: transport pressure
records.fact: The ONS October release identifies transport, especially motor fuels, as the largest upward contributor to the change in annual CPI inflation.
records.analysis: Fuel-intensive businesses may face margin pressure where contracts lack effective cost pass-through. Counsel can assess price adjustment, hardship and supplier renegotiation mechanisms without assuming inflation excuses performance.
records.watch: Next ONS release and evidence of cost pass-through in company results.

records.title: Public offers and admissions to trading regime
records.fact: The new public offers and admissions framework and associated changes to UK listing processes took effect on 19 January 2026, according to the FCA. The FCA also describes a notification requirement for admissions under PRM 1.6.4R.
records.analysis: For equity issuers and advisers, prospectus analysis must begin with the relevant offer/admission route and exceptions under the current regime, rather than recycling old templates.
records.watch: Check the current FCA Handbook and transitional rules before advising on a particular issuance.

records.title: CMA merger procedure guidance
records.fact: The CMA's guidance page identifies a December 2025 version of its merger jurisdiction and procedure guidance. The date here denotes the month of that version, not a claimed commencement day.
records.analysis: Screen UK nexus, jurisdiction and possible review early; agree responsibility for submissions, cooperation and remedy risk in the deal documents. Guidance is not itself legislation.
records.watch: Use the latest version and applicable Enterprise Act provisions.

records.title: Takeover Code scope and transition
records.fact: The Panel’s revised jurisdictional scope has a transition period from 3 February 2025 until 2 February 2027 for certain companies previously covered. A UK adviser alone does not make an offer subject to the Code.
records.analysis: Check incorporation, admission history and transition criteria before selecting the public bid timetable. Do not assume every UK-connected acquisition is a Code transaction.
records.watch: Check the Panel’s current applicability guidance for the specific target.

records.title: PAI Partners / ELEMIS
records.fact: L’Occitane Group and PAI announced an agreement for PAI to acquire British skincare brand ELEMIS. Linklaters subsequently announced its work for the lenders providing acquisition financing.
records.analysis: A sponsor acquisition connects brand valuation and distribution strategy to financing capacity. Counsel must coordinate diligence on IP, distribution and supply arrangements with the financing conditions and acquisition timetable.
records.watch: Completion confirmation and any disclosed financing terms. Do not treat signing as closing.
records.structure: Sponsor acquisition of the skincare business, subject to transaction conditions.
records.financing: Lender-side acquisition financing mandate disclosed; principal amount and facility terms not established.
records.legalWork: Review trademarks, formulation rights, product claims, distribution and retailer change-of-control consents; align acquisition CPs with financing availability and security package.
records.interview: How would you diligence a consumer brand whose value depends on IP, distribution and repeat customers?

records.title: Leita Mobility / Mobico Group
records.fact: The recommended cash acquisition of UK-listed Mobico was announced at 46p per share, with an intended scheme of arrangement. The disclosed equity valuation was approximately £308m and enterprise valuation approximately £2.3bn.
records.analysis: The gap between equity and enterprise valuation makes the capital structure central to the investment thesis. Do not infer net debt from the gap without checking the valuation definitions. A scheme requires its own shareholder and court process; lenders also need certainty on funding and closing.
records.watch: Scheme timetable, applicable approvals and completion announcements.
parties: CMC Group and Asterion Industrial Partners
records.structure: Recommended cash offer intended to be implemented by scheme of arrangement.
records.financing: Clifford Chance disclosed financing work; detailed debt terms not verified. Equity and enterprise valuations are separately disclosed.
records.legalWork: Model equity bridge and existing debt treatment, test cash confirmation and financing conditions, prepare scheme timetable and coordinate regulatory work. Review change-of-control clauses in transport concessions.
records.interview: Why can a £308m equity offer imply a £2.3bn enterprise valuation? Which debt and cash definitions must be checked?

records.title: Nordic Capital / CPP Investments / Ontario Teachers’ — Cary Group
records.fact: CPP Investments and Ontario Teachers’ agreed to join Nordic Capital as owners of Cary Group, which operates in the UK among other markets. Linklaters disclosed a proposed €545m Ontario Teachers’ investment; this is not the overall transaction value.
records.analysis: A consortium structure raises governance questions distinct from the purchase price: reserved matters, future funding, exit rights and alignment between investors with different investment horizons.
records.watch: Regulatory approvals and confirmation of closing; the announced expectation was the first half of 2027.
records.structure: Joint investment by institutional investors alongside existing sponsor.
records.legalWork: Set governance, reserved matters, information and transfer rights; specify funding commitments and exit process. Diligence multi-country operating subsidiaries and local approvals.
records.interview: How do investment horizons of pension funds and a private equity sponsor affect shareholder agreements?

records.title: Goldman Sachs Alternatives / Celnor Group
records.fact: Inflexion announced an agreement to sell a majority stake in UK-based Celnor to Goldman Sachs Alternatives. Inflexion and management are to reinvest. Linklaters disclosed its advice to Goldman Sachs Alternatives.
records.analysis: Reinvestment can align the seller and management with the buyer’s growth strategy, but the documents must address governance, leaver provisions, future capital needs and exit mechanics. A majority investment does not imply acquisition of every share.
records.watch: Closing, subject to the announced timetable, and any publicly disclosed governance arrangements.
records.structure: Majority acquisition with continuing investment by seller and management.
records.legalWork: Negotiate governance and management incentive documents alongside the SPA, review acquisition pipeline and integration risk, identify change-of-control consents in regulated testing and compliance businesses.
records.interview: Why does management rollover create both alignment and potential conflicts?

records.title: RWE / KKR — Vanguard offshore wind projects
records.fact: RWE announced final investment decisions for the UK Vanguard West and East offshore wind projects. The announced combined project investment is approximately £12bn, not an acquisition price or debt facility.
records.analysis: Project economics depend on construction cost, revenue arrangements, grid connection and risk allocation. The investment decision does not eliminate construction risk; advisers must distinguish committed funding, drawdown conditions and completion milestones.
records.watch: Construction, grid connection and financing milestones; distinguish investment approval from operational completion.
records.structure: Offshore wind project investment; not a purchase-price announcement.
records.legalWork: Map procurement, construction, grid and offtake interfaces; consider security, lender step-in and completion support. Model cost overruns and delays rather than assuming investment approval proves funding has been drawn.
records.interview: How do construction and revenue risks change the financing of offshore wind compared with an operating asset?

records.title: New UK renewable power auction
records.fact: The UK government announced a new clean-power renewables auction on 19 November.
records.analysis: Revenue support can improve cash flow predictability for qualifying projects, but winning an auction is not equivalent to securing construction funding. Developers need to test bid economics against financing cost, procurement and delivery risk.
records.watch: Auction results, project-specific contracts and subsequent investment decisions.

records.title: Companies House identity verification: enforcement approach
records.fact: Companies House published its approach to non-compliance with mandatory identity verification. The rollout began in November 2025; applicable deadlines depend on the person’s role and circumstances.
records.analysis: Deal teams should include identity verification and filing readiness in completion and post-completion checklists. A general rollout date is not a substitute for checking the specific statutory deadline and enforcement guidance.
records.watch: Current Companies House guidance for the relevant director or person with significant control.

records.title: LSEG / Octus
records.structure: Cash acquisition of credit intelligence provider.
records.fact: LSEG agreed to buy Octus for US$3.535bn in cash. The transaction extends the group's credit data and analytics offering. LSEG expects closing in H1 2027 subject to regulatory approval.
records.financing: External debt; LSEG expects leverage near the top of its 1.5–2.5x target range at end-2027 under its stated assumptions.
records.regulatory: Regulatory approval is a condition; specific authority decisions are not established here.
records.financialAdvisers: Morgan Stanley (lead) and Barclays for LSEG; Evercore and Goldman Sachs for Octus shareholders.
records.analysis: Subscription credit intelligence can complement LSEG's data business. The buyer's forecasts are not guarantees: debt-financed growth raises leverage and integration risk.
records.legalWork: Diligence rights to financial data, contractual licences, IP, privacy and customer change-of-control terms; coordinate financing, regulatory conditions and cross-border acquisition documentation.
records.watch: Regulatory decisions, debt financing and closing confirmation.
records.interview: How could a debt-funded data acquisition affect both recurring revenue and the buyer’s leverage?

records.title: IFM Investors / Associated British Ports stakes
records.structure: Sale of two existing institutional shareholdings: 33.9% and 30%.
records.fact: Linklaters disclosed agreements to sell the CPP Investments and OMERS stakes to an IFM-managed fund. ABP operates 19 UK port facilities; completion was expected in H1 2027 subject to conditions.
records.analysis: Long-life infrastructure assets may appeal to institutional investors seeking cash flows, but capital-intensive port operations create maintenance, concession and environmental exposure.
records.legalWork: Examine shareholder and financing agreements, change-of-control provisions, land and port rights, antitrust and foreign-investment screening. Do not infer that a particular approval is mandatory without reviewing the actual structure.
records.regulatory: Conditions disclosed in broad terms only; individual approval status not established.
records.watch: Conditions, financing and closing announcement.
records.interview: How do port infrastructure risks differ from a software acquisition?

records.title: Associated British Ports / £300m infrastructure facility
parties: Bank of America London branch, Lloyds and NatWest
records.structure: Term facility combining public and private capital.
records.fact: The National Wealth Fund announced a £200m commitment on 3 June; Linklaters subsequently disclosed a £300m overall term facility including £100m from commercial banks.
records.financing: Public and private lenders fund a port investment programme. Drawdowns, maturity and pricing are not established in this record.
records.analysis: Combining public and commercial capital can support infrastructure with significant upfront costs. Lender objectives may differ, so permitted use and reporting are material.
records.legalWork: Negotiate facility documentation, conditions to utilisation, representations, covenants and coordination among lenders; test permitted investment use and reporting requirements.
records.watch: Drawdown and project delivery announcements.
records.interview: How does a £300m committed facility differ from £300m of drawn debt?

records.title: UK Logistics 2026-3 / £603m CMBS
records.structure: Commercial mortgage-backed notes backed by a portion of a logistics property financing.
records.fact: Clifford Chance disclosed completion of securitisation of £603m of financing secured against 39 logistics and industrial properties in England and Wales.
records.financing: Commercial mortgage-backed note issuance; tranche details not established in this record.
records.analysis: Property cash flows and valuation affect credit risk. Securitisation distributes mortgage exposure to investors, but does not eliminate default or refinancing risks.
records.legalWork: Review loan transfer, security, issuer structure, servicing, cash-flow waterfall, disclosure and tax; coordinate UK real estate and securities advice across jurisdictions.
records.watch: Note documentation and property performance where publicly available.
records.interview: How does a CMBS differ from a direct bilateral property loan?

timeline.event: Completed issuance reported by transaction counsel

advisers.scope: Arrangers, managers, loan sellers and issuer lenders

records.title: Standard Chartered / US$200m digitally native notes
records.structure: Floating-rate digitally native notes due 2029.
records.fact: Clifford Chance reported the UK bank's US$200m issuance through Euroclear's digital issuance infrastructure; application was made for admission to London's International Securities Market.
records.analysis: Digital settlement infrastructure can change operational processes without eliminating ordinary debt and securities-law obligations.
records.legalWork: Examine issuance and settlement arrangements, title and payment mechanics, continuity provisions, disclosure and admission requirements. Distinguish application for admission from actual admission.
records.watch: Further issuances and evidence of completed admission.
records.interview: What legal and operational risks remain when a bond is issued using distributed ledger infrastructure?

records.title: Drax / Bluefield Solar Income Fund
records.structure: Acquisition of renewable infrastructure investment fund.
records.fact: Drax confirms completion effective 31 July. Its later trading update reports £561m consideration and £1.082bn enterprise value.

values.label: Enterprise value reported in trading update

records.analysis: Acquiring operating renewable assets changes the buyer's generation mix and introduces portfolio-specific debt, power-price and asset performance exposure.
records.legalWork: Review project SPV debt, change-of-control provisions, revenue support contracts, generation asset title and integration. Distinguish the acquisition consideration from enterprise valuation.
records.watch: Operating performance and integration disclosures.
records.interview: Why might a renewable portfolio's enterprise value be substantially greater than its equity consideration?

records.title: Vivisol / Air Liquide UK home oxygen business
parties: Air Liquide UK home oxygen services business
records.structure: Proposed acquisition under CMA review; consideration and definitive structure not established.
records.fact: CMA announced possible competition harm and a reference unless acceptable undertakings are offered.
records.regulatory: CMA announced possible competition harm and a reference unless acceptable undertakings are offered.
records.analysis: The published procedural milestone identifies regulatory risk, not a completed or prohibited transaction. Transaction economics require separate issuer or party evidence.
records.legalWork: Assess regional supply and tender alternatives, continuity of patient services and viability of possible remedies; do not assume divestment terms.
records.watch: Subsequent CMA decision or formal start.
records.interview: Why is continuity of supply important when considering remedies in healthcare?

records.title: FirstCash / Ramsdens
records.structure: Proposed acquisition under CMA review; consideration and definitive structure not established.
records.fact: CMA launched its formal inquiry into the anticipated acquisition on 26 October.
records.regulatory: CMA launched its formal inquiry into the anticipated acquisition on 26 October.
records.analysis: The published procedural milestone identifies regulatory risk, not a completed or prohibited transaction. Transaction economics require separate issuer or party evidence.
records.legalWork: Assess market overlap in relevant consumer financial services, local competition and any separate regulatory requirements; map completion conditions.
records.watch: 2026-12-22 — subject to extensions
records.interview: How can local market competition affect a national acquisition?

records.title: Prologis / SEGRO
records.structure: Proposed acquisition under CMA review; consideration and definitive structure not established.
records.fact: CMA opened an invitation to comment on the anticipated acquisition; formal Phase 1 start was listed as to be confirmed.
records.regulatory: CMA opened an invitation to comment on the anticipated acquisition; formal Phase 1 start was listed as to be confirmed.
records.analysis: The published procedural milestone identifies regulatory risk, not a completed or prohibited transaction. Transaction economics require separate issuer or party evidence.
records.legalWork: Assess logistics property market definition, customer alternatives and geographic overlap; avoid equating pre-notification with formal inquiry.
records.watch: Subsequent CMA decision or formal start.
records.interview: Why might geographic market definition matter for warehouse tenants?

records.title: PRA publishes general insurance stress test results
records.fact: The PRA published results of its 2026 dynamic general insurance stress test on 23 November. The exercise examined how participating insurers respond to severe shocks; it was designed to examine crisis management as well as financial resilience.
records.analysis: Insurance clients face interconnected exposures across underwriting, reinsurance, liquidity and counterparty risk. Legal teams can use stress scenarios to test recovery governance, reinsurance contract terms and operational escalation, not treat the exercise as a guarantee of solvency.
records.watch: PRA follow-up and firm-level risk management responses. No individual insurer capital conclusion is inferred.

records.title: £700m Strategic Sites Accelerator
records.fact: Government announced a programme of about £700m in debt, equity and targeted grants to unlock up to ten major industrial and commercial sites. This is programme-level funding, not a completed investment in any named site.
records.analysis: Reducing planning, infrastructure and financing barriers can make development sites investable. Counsel will need to distinguish public commitments from private investment, examine grant and subsidy conditions, land rights, procurement and the sequencing of financing and development milestones.
records.watch: Site selection, grant or funding decisions and evidence of private capital commitments.

records.title: Modernising corporate reporting: consultation
records.fact: The government opened a consultation on modernising the corporate reporting framework on 7 September. Its proposals include reconsidering the existing distributable-profits and capital-maintenance regime.
records.analysis: If adopted, a solvency-oriented approach could change how boards evaluate distributions and capital transactions. Existing law remains applicable until changes are enacted and in force. Companies should review reporting and governance processes without assuming that proposals are binding.
records.watch: Consultation closes 30 November 2026; monitor response, legislation and commencement.

records.title: FCA Primary Market Bulletin 67: proposed technical-note changes
records.fact: GC26/8 proposes updates to technical notes on prospectus exemptions and supplements, and revocation of other guidance following rule changes. The consultation is not itself a final amendment to binding rules.
records.analysis: Issuer counsel should check the operative PRM rules and current guidance when assessing the need for a prospectus or supplement. Updating drafting precedents based solely on proposed notes risks prematurely applying a change.
records.watch: Comments due 9 December 2026; monitor finalised guidance.

records.title: FCA review of investment firms prudential regime
records.status: Call for evidence; no rule change
records.fact: The FCA is seeking views on the IFPR, including ICARA, group consolidation, proportionality and wind-down planning. It expects to consult on possible amendments in 2027.
records.analysis: Investment firms should distinguish the existing prudential regime from the proposed review. A group restructuring or acquisition can change the risk perimeter and capital and liquidity analysis, so regulatory due diligence needs current group-level data.
records.watch: Feedback deadline 20 January 2027; monitor proposed changes. Existing transitional own-funds provisions expire on 31 December 2026, according to the FCA.

lessons.title: Enterprise value, equity value and cash flow
lessons.body: Enterprise value measures the operating business under a specified valuation convention. In a simplified cash-free, debt-free deal, equity value equals enterprise value less debt plus cash. Actual price adjustments depend on the agreed definitions of cash, debt, debt-like items and working capital. EBITDA is not cash flow: capital expenditure, tax and working capital may consume cash.
lessons.scenario: A business has £120m enterprise value, £35m debt and £5m cash. Ignoring other adjustments, what equity price is implied?
lessons.explanation: £120m − £35m + £5m = £90m. The SPA must specify which items count as cash and debt.

lessons.title: Debt, interest rates and covenants
lessons.body: Floating-rate borrowing commonly references a benchmark plus margin. Rate rises can reduce interest cover, increase refinancing pressure and reduce the debt a buyer can service. Fixed-rate debt and hedging may change the impact. A covenant breach depends on the precise financial definitions, test dates and cure rights, not on a headline rate alone.
lessons.scenario: A borrower has £80m of unhedged floating-rate debt. Assuming immediate full pass-through, what is the additional annual interest from a 25bp rise?

lessons.title: UK merger control and remedies
lessons.body: The UK merger regime is generally voluntary, but the CMA may investigate qualifying anticipated or completed transactions. Review can lead to clearance, commitments, deeper investigation or prohibition. Contractual closing conditions, long-stop dates and risk allocation need to reflect the transaction's particular facts and any separate mandatory regimes.
lessons.scenario: A buyer completes a UK transaction before the CMA reviews it. Which statement is safest?
options: The CMA may still review a qualifying completed merger
Only the seller faces regulatory risk
lessons.explanation: A qualifying completed merger may still be reviewed; the Co-operative case provides a concrete illustration.

lessons.title: Public M&A and capital markets
lessons.body: A public takeover and an equity issuance solve different commercial problems. Before planning a public acquisition, establish whether the Takeover Code applies; before a capital raising, identify the market, admission route, offer and applicable prospectus rules. Regulatory timetables, disclosure and execution risk affect the financing plan.
lessons.scenario: A foreign bidder retains a London law firm to acquire a foreign private company. Does that alone establish Takeover Code jurisdiction?
options: No; test the target and Code scope
Yes, if counsel is Magic Circle
lessons.explanation: The location of an adviser is not a standalone test of the Code’s applicability.

lessons.title: How clients make money
lessons.body: Revenue is sales before expenses; profit depends on costs and accounting rules. Operating cash flow also reflects collection and payment timing. A high-growth company can be profitable on paper but short of cash. Ask what customers pay for, what drives costs, how working capital behaves and what regulation constrains the business.
lessons.scenario: Sales rise but customers take much longer to pay. What can happen?
options: Cash flow can weaken despite higher revenue
lessons.explanation: Receivables tie up cash. A profitable business may still need working-capital finance.

lessons.title: Commercial interview reasoning
lessons.body: Start with a specific, dated fact. Identify the client and its commercial objective, trace the financial or operational impact, identify legal work and risks, then state what evidence could change your view. Avoid pretending that every issue has the same impact on all clients.
lessons.scenario: A buyer is concerned about a competition remedy. Which response demonstrates the strongest reasoning?
options: Test the remedy’s impact on synergies, financing and closing conditions
lessons.explanation: The best answer links a concrete regulatory outcome to deal economics and legal drafting. This is original practice material, not an employer question.

lessons.title: Private equity and management rollover
lessons.body: Sponsors seek returns through operating improvements, growth, capital structure and eventual exit. Rollover means existing investors or management reinvest some proceeds or retain an interest. Review shareholder rights, dilution, incentives, transfer restrictions and exit arrangements. The investment’s value and the target’s enterprise value are different concepts.
lessons.scenario: A sponsor buys a majority stake and management reinvests. What is a priority alongside the SPA?
options: Assume management has no continuing rights
Negotiate governance, incentives and exit rights
Treat all debt as seller proceeds
Assume the business has already been sold
lessons.explanation: Continuing shareholders need a workable governance and exit framework, distinct from the acquisition terms.

lessons.title: Infrastructure and project finance
lessons.body: Project finance often relies on cash flows of a project company, with limited or non-recourse structures depending on the agreed financing. Construction, operating, revenue and political risks are allocated across contracts, insurance, security and sponsor support. A final investment decision is not the same as financial close or operational completion.
lessons.scenario: An offshore wind development has a final investment decision. What can you safely conclude?
options: The investment has been approved; delivery and funding milestones still matter
lessons.explanation: An investment decision is distinct from completion, drawdown and commissioning.

lessons.title: Corporate governance and completion readiness
lessons.body: Completion involves more than payment: approvals, executed documents, registers, appointments and filings may matter. In UK transactions the precise obligations depend on company type, structure and the law in force. Check current Companies House identity-verification requirements for directors and persons with significant control rather than applying one deadline to everyone.
lessons.scenario: A director will be appointed at completion. Which approach is best?
options: Ignore identity verification until a problem occurs
Check the applicable verification requirement and filing sequence
Assume all directors had one identical deadline
Treat verification as a competition-law approval
lessons.explanation: Verification and filing readiness should be checked against the applicable rules for the individual and transaction.

lessons.title: UK national security screening
lessons.body: The National Security and Investment Act creates a distinct national security review regime. Certain qualifying acquisitions of control over entities in specified sectors require mandatory notification. Asset acquisitions are not subject to mandatory notification but may be called in. Competition and national security reviews require separate analysis.
lessons.scenario: An acquisition is cleared by the CMA on competition grounds. Does that establish NSI clearance?
options: No; separately assess NSI jurisdiction and any notification requirement
Yes if both parties are British
Only if the deal is a share purchase
lessons.explanation: The regimes serve different purposes and must be assessed separately.

lessons.title: Securitisation and credit risk
lessons.body: A securitisation uses a financing structure in which investors are paid from a pool of underlying exposures, subject to contractual priorities. Analyse asset transfer, security, servicing, cash-flow waterfalls, credit enhancement and insolvency risk. CMBS can expose investors to property cash flow and refinancing risk.
lessons.scenario: A CMBS issuer sells senior and junior notes. Does securitisation eliminate borrower default risk?
options: No; losses are allocated through the contractual structure
lessons.explanation: The structure allocates credit risk rather than making the underlying exposure risk-free.

lessons.title: Schemes of arrangement and deal certainty
lessons.body: A scheme of arrangement is a court-supervised process. A public takeover implemented by scheme typically requires the relevant shareholder approvals and court sanction, alongside satisfaction of applicable offer conditions. Check the transaction documents and the relevant Companies Act and Takeover Code provisions.
lessons.scenario: A scheme has shareholder support but merger clearance is outstanding. Which conclusion is sound?
options: A closing condition may remain outstanding
